question.worked_solution:
We start by recalling the conversion table for mass units. 

| Name | Symbol | Conversion |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Kilogram | $\textrm{kg}$ | $1\,\textrm{kg} = 1\,000\,\textrm{g}$ |
| Gram | $\textrm{g}$ | Base Unit |
| Milligram | $\textrm{mg}$ | $1\,000\,\textrm{mg} = 1\,\textrm{g}$ |

There are $1000\,\textrm g$ per $\textrm{kg},$ which we can write as follows:

$$
\dfrac{1000\,\textrm g}{\textrm{kg}}
$$

This is our conversion factor.

Now, multiplying $0.2\,\textrm{kg}$ by our conversion factor, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}0.2\,\text{kg} & =0.2\,\text{kg}\cdot \frac{1\,000\,\text{g}}{\text{kg}} \\  & =0.2\,\cancel{\text{kg}}\cdot \frac{1\,000\,\text{g}}{\cancel{\text{kg}}} \\  & =0.2\cdot 1\,000\,\text{g} \\  & =200\,\text{g}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $0.2\,\textrm{kg}$ is equivalent to $200 \,\text{g}.$
